'''Chava Lifshitz''' ({{Langx|he|חוה ליפשיץ}}; March 26, 1936 – March 1, 2005), née '''Eva Wolf''', was an Austrian-Israeli [[chemist]] who was best known for her contributions to [[mass spectrometry]] and the gas-phase chemistry of ions. She was awarded the Israel Chemical Society Prize for Outstanding Scientist in 2003.

== Early life and education ==
Lifshitz was born Eva Wolf in [[Vienna]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Katalog der Deutschen Nationalbibliothek|url=https://portal.dnb.de/opac/showFullRecord?currentResultId=%22133914925%22&any&currentPosition=1#:~:text=http://d-nb.info/gnd/133914925|access-date=2021-09-23|website=portal.dnb.de}}</ref> She was born to an upper middle class family. Her father, Salomon Wolf worked as a lawyer in Vienna. When Austria was annexed into [[Nazi Germany]], her father emigrated to [[Eretz Yisrael]], and their names became [[Hebrew language|Hebrew]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Chava Lifshitz, 1936—2005|url=https://theochem.weizmann.ac.il/chava.html|access-date=2021-09-23|website=theochem.weizmann.ac.il}}</ref> She performed well at school and had piano lessons with composer [[Paul Ben-Haim]].{{citation needed|date=September 2021}} Lifschitz was an undergraduate student in chemistry at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], where she was involved with a program that involved military service.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|date=July 1, 2006|title=Curriculum Vitae for Chava Lifshitz|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/full/10.1021/jp068045v|journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry A|volume=110|issue=27|pages=8238|doi=10.1021/jp068045v|bibcode=2006JPCA..110.8238. |issn=1089-5639|url-access=subscription}}</ref> She remained at the Hebrew University for doctoral studies, where she studied isotope effects in radiation chemistry.<ref name=":1" /> During her graduate studies she met her future husband, Assa Lifshitz.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Assa Lifshitz|url=https://chemistry.huji.ac.il/Assa|access-date=2021-09-23|website=chemistry.huji.ac.il|language=en}}</ref> Lifshitz was a postdoctoral scholar with [[Franklin A. Long]] at [[Cornell University]], where she started to work with mass spectrometry and unimolecular fragmentations of polyatomic ions.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|date=July 1, 2006|title=Biography of Chava Lifshitz|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/full/10.1021/jp068040y|journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry A|volume=110|issue=27|pages=8235–8237|doi=10.1021/jp068040y|pmid=16821804 |issn=1089-5639|last1=Baer |first1=T. |last2=Laskin |first2=J. |bibcode=2006JPCA..110.8235. |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Research career ==
In 1963 Lifshitz returned to the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, where she established her own independent research group and was appointed Professor in 1976.<ref name=":1" /> Lifshitz worked as a visiting scientist at [[Argonne National Laboratory]], where she worked on [[VUV (radiation)|VUV]] photoionisation mass spectrometry.<ref name=":2" /> She also worked as a visiting scientist at [[Cornell University]] and [[Wright-Patterson Air Force Base]].<ref name=":2"/> In 1986 Lifshitz was appointed a Brotherton Research Professor at the [[University of Leeds]], where she started working on biomolecules and reaction dynamics.  Lifshitz held various senior positions at the Hebrew University, including Chair of the Chemistry Division, head of the [[Mass spectrometry]] laboratory and member of the Israel Board of higher Education.<ref name=":1" /> She was named the Archie and Markorie Sherman Professor of Chemistry in 1989.<ref name=":1" /> Lifshitz worked on [[mass spectrometry]] and the gas-phase chemistry of ions.

== Awards and honors ==
* 1985: [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology]] Kolthoff Prize<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chava Lifshitz, 1936—2005|url=https://theochem.weizmann.ac.il/chava.html|access-date=2021-09-23|website=theochem.weizmann.ac.il}}</ref>
* 1991: [[:de:Max-Planck-Forschungspreis|Max Planck Research Prize]] with [[Helmut Schwarz]]<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Socialist International Women|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1163/1570-6664_iyb_sim_org_39339|access-date=2021-09-23|website=International Year Book and Statesmen's Who's Who|doi=10.1163/1570-6664_iyb_sim_org_39339 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>
* 1991: President of the Israel Society for Mass Spectrometry<ref name=":1" />
* 2003: Israel Chemical Society Prize for Outstanding Scientist<ref>{{Cite web|title=Outstanding Scientist|url=https://www.chemistry.org.il/outstanding-scientist|access-date=2021-09-23|website=ics-website|language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Chava and Assa Lifshitz had three children, Ron, Donna and Orna Lifshitz. She held a long-term cancer diagnosis, which she lived with for over twenty years.<ref name=":0" />
